notes: Cross-verse consistency. αὐτόν is the accusative subject of τεθνηκέναι, which the chapter elsewhere realizes by the English subject word (αὐτούς → they at 14.1, ἡμᾶς → we at 14.22), and σύρω's object is unexpressed in Greek, so the him English transitivity requires is a rule 7 helper on ἔσυρον, as of it is on συνιδόντες at 14.6 and ἀκούσαντες at 14.14 and them is on παρακαλοῦντες at 14.22. The accepted alignment gave both him and he to αὐτόν and left the finite verb with no object, which is the one place in the chapter where a supplied argument was assigned to a token that does not license it. Only these two units change; every other unit is as the verse pass returned it.
